conclusions: With the unchanged six-word, 0.7 lexical confidence, speech support and repeat-timing gates, small.en q5_1 produces reliable inserted-dialogue runs 2/6/7 on both CPU and Metal-preferred workers. The earlier native-converted base.en runs were 4/3/2.
Aligned-dialogue controls still match the SRT. Quiet controls never qualify as repeated absent speech; one quiet result is rejected for invalid timestamps on both profiles.

CPU p95 4.142 s exceeds the frozen 3 s budget. Reported Metal-preferred inference p95 is 0.607 s, but the first active request takes 14.254 s including unisolated setup/polling. Backend preference does not independently prove physical GPU use.

The full active late-insertion replay still learns only one region and fails recovery. A recognized window contains two ignored multiword annotation segments whose split normalization discards temporal alignment; subsequent timing checks remain relevant.
limitations: Consumed development audio only. The overlapping word comparison uses diagnostic ASCII normalization; it is not a production absence learner.
